* fix(cli): gen2-migration forward-direction function grants avoid circular deps

The generate command emitted a function's access to auth and storage as
reverse-direction constructs: `access: (allow) => [allow.resource(fn).to([...])]`
on defineAuth, and `allow.resource(fn)` entries in the defineStorage access
block. Both make the auth/storage stack reference the function's role, i.e. an
`auth -> function` / `storage -> function` cross-stack dependency. When the same
function also accesses another category (e.g. data or storage) the usual
`data -> auth` / `storage -> auth` edges close a cross-stack cycle, and the
generated Gen2 app fails to deploy with CloudformationStackCircularDependencyError.
Setting resourceGroupName only co-locates resources and cannot break a genuine
cross-category cycle.

Emit the grants in the forward direction in backend.ts instead, on the underlying
CDK constructs, so the dependency stays `function -> auth` / `function -> storage`:

- auth: `backend.auth.resources.userPool.grant(backend.<fn>.resources.lambda, ...)`
  with a documented Amplify-permission -> cognito-idp action mapping (the CDK grant
  works on raw IAM actions rather than Amplify permission names).
- storage: `backend.storage.resources.bucket.grant{Read,Write,ReadWrite,Delete}(...)`,
  choosing the narrowest grant that covers the consolidated permission set.

Identity-based storage access (guest / authenticated / group) is unchanged and
still rendered as the per-path defineStorage access block; a bucket whose only
Gen1 access was function access now emits no access block at all.

Regenerated the fitness-tracker, media-vault, and store-locator migration-app
snapshots to reflect the forward-direction output.

* fix(amplify-migration): harden trigger auth-access path and consolidate grants

Address review follow-ups on the gen2-migration trigger-vs-non-trigger auth
access partition:

- Validate every interpolated function/trigger identifier up front in
  AuthGenerator.execute(), so the trigger-access path is guarded against
  invalid JS identifiers the same way the non-trigger grant path and the S3
  builder already are.
- Warn when an auth-trigger function also has storage/data access: the trigger
  edge plus the function's storage/data grants can form a deploy-time circular
  dependency the auth-grant partition alone cannot break. Surfaced from the
  function generator, which is the per-function authority on cross-category
  access.
- Run the unknown-permission warning over all registered auth access (trigger
  and non-trigger), not just the non-trigger subset, so an unmapped Gen1
  permission on a trigger is not emitted silently.
- Consolidate each function's auth permissions into a single deduped, sorted
  allow.resource(fn).to([...]) rule, matching the forward grant builder and
  emitting fewer Policy constructs.
- Route the always-present Tags import through the deduped/sorted named-import
  map so a future aws-cdk-lib symbol cannot emit a duplicate import.

Adds trigger-path tests for identifier validation and the unknown-permission
warning, a test for the trigger-with-storage cycle warning, and backend
renderer tests asserting the aws-iam import appears with grants and is omitted
without. Regenerates the store-locator snapshot for the consolidated grant.

* fix(cli): harden trigger cycle warning and its tests

Count analytics (Kinesis) access in the auth-trigger cycle signal, and
only count data/analytics grants for nodejs runtimes, since non-JS
functions surface those grants as manual-migration notes rather than
emitting them. Storage access still always counts.

Add a FunctionGenerator test covering the call site that marks the
auth generator (JS runtime marks, non-JS does not), focused tests for
access-rule consolidation (duplicate registration and all-false
permissions), and a trigger-only invalid-identifier test. Fix the
backend renderer test to use the aws-cdk-lib/aws-iam source that the
